reviewer: Separate Claude (Opus 5.5) review agent, independent of the extractor; no human review claimed
scope: Independent review of the Ahlmann-Eltze et al. 2025 derived batch for use-case-genetic-perturbation-response: 131 records (59 results with derivation, 30 evaluations, 11 configurations, 13 claims including 4 relevance judgements, 5 sources, 4 datasets, 4 protocols, 3 methods, 2 models). The article XML and the four Source Data workbooks were re-downloaded and match their recorded SHA-256. scripts/omics/derive/ahlmann_eltze_2025.py (sha256 452a7a7aaab7e4965142de87ed9f00209a6d9664760919cb39b921bb45aec45c) was rerun on the fresh downloads and its output equals derived-values.jsonl; all 59 means and row counts were recomputed with a separate openpyxl reader and match. Changes are listed in docs/reviews/use-cases/genetic-perturbation-response-2026-10-11.md.
limitations: Automated review by a Claude agent; not human scientific review and not reproduction of any model run.
The values are means computed from the authors' Source Data; the paper prints none, so no printed number was available to check against.
Fig. 2c, Fig. 1c, Extended Data Fig. 2b, 4, 8b and 10 were not checked beyond confirming they were not extracted.
Judgement pins are not set; the integrator runs use-cases:repin after the records are in the store.
batch.jsonl and claims.csv now differ from the output of extract/build_batch.py; do not regenerate them.

errors.message: Every printed_value, numeric_value, row_count, row_filter, input hash, aggregation quote and locator and script hash matches the recomputation and the article.
Origin split is right: the authors' own or adopted baselines are author_reported; the seven third-party models are independent_paper. None is rewire_run or paper_compilation.
unit_detail no longer asserts a log transform, which the article states only for the Norman data.
Noted that paragraph 16 states the finding for the single-perturbation benchmark as a whole, not per dataset.
Fig. 2c citation attached to the paragraph 17 statement; paragraph 18 cites no figure.
UCE and scBERT ground-truth embedding caveat added to the single-perturbation judgements and protocols; scBERT named in the Norman protocol.
Name and descriptions limited to what the article states.
First evidence concern now records that using split 1 only would change the means by up to 0.61 (L2) and 0.06 (Pearson delta) and the top model on Adamson and Replogle RPE1.
